_comment: Harness config. limits: the Big-plan spend caps (USD) the proxy enforces per workflow run and per rolling week. models: what CodeAF may use, served to it by `harness proxy` as an OpenRouter-shaped catalog; prices are USD per million tokens, from https://synthetic.new/pricing, checked 2026-10-17. input/output/cache_read are the SUBSCRIPTION rates, which draw down the weekly credit; api_input/api_cached/api_output are the API list rates, what usage past the quota (overage) costs. 'id' is what CodeAF sees; 'upstream' is the synthetic.new model id. 'max_concurrent': how many calls the factory sends each model at once, the proxy queuing calls past it. synthetic.new no longer has a fixed per-model cap (October 2026 pricing change: concurrency is by plan priority, Big highest, with throttling to protect the service), so 8 is our own first step up from the old cap of 2, raised further only while upstream 429s stay rare; CodeAF retries a 429. queue.max_parallel_runs is how many CodeAF runs the queue may have going at once; each run gets its own slice of every model's max_concurrent (perRunSlots: max(1, max_concurrent/max_parallel_runs), what task.parallel is set to) and its own worker seat, chosen by the lane the queue assigns. searches_per_run caps the web-search calls (harness search, POST /v2/search) one run may forward to synthetic.new; search is in the plan and draws no credit, but the cap walls off a runaway loop (issue #58). planner (issue #61): when the queue sees fewer than min_backlog codeaf-queued issues open and no plan run started within min_hours, harness plan-check tells the queue job to dispatch one CodeAF run in plan mode (a read-only pass whose proposals are labelled codeaf-proposed, never codeaf-queued); max_proposals caps what one plan run may propose. alerts (issue #131): the thresholds the model-stats routine alerts on. They are config and not code because a threshold is a judgement about the service, not a fact about the code: synthetic.new can degrade, a plan can change, and the owner must be able to move a threshold in a reviewed config file without a code change. Every field is optional and means the issue #131 value when the block is absent, so a models.json written before the block still loads; main.go's validator refuses an absurd value naming the field. hour_calls is how many calls an hour needs before its first-token p50 is judged at all; ttft_p50_ratio compares an hour's p50 against the model's own trailing baseline (ttft_p50_ratio_baseline_hours) and ttft_p90_ms alerts on a p90 above 15 s. The decode figures count only completions of decode_min_tokens or more, so a short call measures its own overhead rather than throughput, and decode_ratio alerts when decode p50 drops below that fraction of the baseline over decode_baseline_hours. stall_gap_ms is the silence between streamed lines that counts as a stall, and stall_pct the share of turns carrying one that alerts. rate_429_pct is the rate above which the factory should lower max_concurrent rather than raise it; reject_pct is the share of hostile or unusable rows refused before the report is built. slot_waits_per_run alerts on a run that queued for a model slot more often than that, and any abandoned wait alerts whatever it says. window_hours is the default window the routine reports over.

alerts._comment: Thresholds the model-stats routine alerts on (issue #131). Each field is optional: an absent block, or a field this file does not carry, uses the issue #131 value the validator in main.go fills in, so a models.json written before this block still loads and still alerts. A count-shaped field written as 0 is refused, not defaulted (a written 0 would silently disable its alert); a percentage or ratio written as 0 means its default, the same as leaving it out. Percentages are percent, not fractions: 1.0 is one percent.

limits.plan_note: Big plan $90/mo. synthetic.new reports the weekly credit itself (GET /v2/quotas weeklyTokenLimit.maxCredits: $22.17 at subscription rates, regenerating about $0.44 every 3h22m), and the owner's other workloads draw on the same quota. All figures and caps here are at the API list (overage) prices, the owner's decision on 2026-10-20: CostOf prices calls at api_*; the input/output/cache_read subscription rates are reference only. weekly_credit_usd 100 is maxCredits x 4.5, the measured overage/subscription ratio for the factory's model mix (2026-10-17..19; DeepSeek alone is ~7.9x); it only paces the queue. The hard stop is synthetic.new's own percentRemaining: with overage_usd 0 the proxy refuses below min_credit_percent (25, leaving a quarter of the week for the owner's other workloads), re-reading /v2/quotas every 5 minutes. run_credit_usd 5 is about 2.5x the most expensive run seen at overage prices ($1.97). overage_usd 0 = stop rather than pay past the quota.

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash (synthetic.new)
models.efforts_note: low, minimal and medium are sent as medium (owner's decision, 2026-10-17): measured on a real multi-step Go edit-and-test task (issue #24, 3 repeats per case) medium saved 19.3% median completion tokens and 17.8% median wall time at equal correctness, and about 72% of this model's output is reasoning. low is never sent raw: GLM returns empty answers at low

models.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 10/17 checkpoint (synthetic.new)
models.efforts_note: role experiment: never picked by a lane until an experiment shows it beats deepseek-v4.1-flash. Added 2026-10-20 from synthetic.new's /openai/v1/models: same API prices, context and efforts as deepseek-v4.1-flash; its subscription rates are assumed equal (not published).

models.name: GLM-5.3 (synthetic.new)
models.efforts_note: low, minimal and medium are all sent as medium: equal correctness (3/3 vs 3/3, 0 empty answers, 0 malformed tool calls) and a real saving (median completion 1332->854, i.e. 35.9% fewer; median wall 26.3->17.8 s, 32.1% less), so medium is sent raw to synthetic.new; low is still never sent raw because GLM returns an empty answer (tested 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-16; measured 2026-10-17, results.md, issue #24)

models.name: Kimi-K3 (synthetic.new)
models.efforts_note: role experiment: never picked by a lane, only by a model-experiment profile (experiments.json). Prices from https://synthetic.new/pricing/models, 2026-10-17. Whether it honours reasoning_effort is unverified.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, infinite mode (synthetic.new)
models.efforts_note: role experiment: never picked by a lane. synthetic.new's infinite mode (Big plan, beta): the same DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights, free and not counted against the weekly credit, but much slower, with long pauses mid-stream; requests must stream. Prices are 0 because it draws no credit.
